So, when you rub two insulating materials together, electrons move from one to the other. The material that picks up those extra electrons gets a negative charge. What happens to the material that loses those electrons?

turns.reply: When one object is negative and another is positive, they pull towards each other — that's called attraction. What happens when both objects are negative?

Now imagine you walk across a carpet and electrons rub off onto you, so you become negatively charged all over. What happens between all those negative charges on your body?
